**What it actually does:** GETASAP operates three interlocking product lines: (1) Same-Day Produce Distribution — direct-from-farm sourcing with global cold-chain infrastructure, delivering to thousands of restaurant and retail locations with an order-by-midnight/on-shelves-by-afternoon SLA; (2) AI-Native Freight Brokerage & Fleet Scheduling — automated load booking, rate negotiation, and truck dispatch for reefer LTL/FTL, powered by a VoiceAI Dispatch module that conducts AI-driven outbound calls to fill open calendar days and negotiate rates; (3) Demand Intelligence — a retail-facing SaaS dashboard providing demand forecasting (94%+ confidence shown in demo UI), waste reduction recommendations, inventory visibility, and automated replenishment suggestions per SKU.

### Product

Lanesurf is an AI-powered freight broker automation platform that replaces human carrier sales reps with AI agents capable of conducting outbound calls, emails, and texts to carriers simultaneously, as well as handling inbound carrier communications. The core workflow covers three stages: (1) Source — AI agents identify nearby empty trucks, blast the broker's entire carrier list in parallel across all communication channels, collect and compare rate quotes; (2) Book — AI confirms load details, negotiates rates autonomously, and executes booking; (3) Track — AI monitors ETAs, contacts drivers for real-time status, flags delays, and escalates with context to human reps. The technology stack centers on a self-described 'self-improving voice AI stack' tuned for logistics-specific challenges: noisy phone calls, compliance verification (MC vetting integrated with existing compliance portals), exception handling, and multi-turn conversation context retention across a load cycle. The system ingests broker SOPs or existing rep call recordings to configure agent behavior and negotiation thresholds, enabling a degree of brokerage-specific customization. Integration is lightweight — brokers can start with an Excel file of loads and achieve full TMS integration in under 10 days, connecting with major TMS platforms, load boards, compliance portals, and CRMs. Security posture includes SOC 2 Type II certification, AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, MFA, and role-based access controls. Key self-reported performance metrics: 60–80% of loads booked via AI-sourced capacity, 8–10% better buy rates per load, and 4+ hours of manual effort saved per rep per day. A notable early enterprise traction signal is the rollout of Lanesurf across Logistic Dynamics (LDi), a network of 130+ offices. The product is live and selling, with a demo environment available. Founded in 2025 by Pratham Bansal and Sarthak Singh Chauhan (both IIT Delhi engineers with prior ML inference and enterprise AI deployment backgrounds), the company is part of YC Summer 2025 with a team of 11 based in San Francisco. Differentiation versus incumbent load boards (DAT, Truckstop) and early AI freight tools lies in the full-cycle agentic workflow — replacing human reps rather than augmenting search — combined with phone-call capability (voice AI), parallel multi-carrier outreach, and embedded compliance checking. The moat is moderate at this stage: the 'self-improving' voice AI trained on logistics-specific conversations and the workflow data accumulated across bookings could compound, but the core enabling technology (LLM-based voice agents, API integrations) is replicable by well-resourced competitors.

### Risk

**Competition:** Lanesurf operates in a rapidly crowding AI-for-freight-brokerage space. Established incumbents — C.H. Robinson (30+ generative AI agents automating 3M+ tasks), Uber Freight (LLM-powered 30-agent network), RXO, and TQL — are aggressively automating their own carrier procurement workflows, giving them embedded customer relationships and scale advantages Lanesurf cannot easily match. Directly competing point-solutions include LunaPath (AI carrier call agents) and others catalogued in broker AI tool roundups, all targeting the same mid-market broker pain point. Large load boards (DAT, Truckstop) are also expanding automation.

**Current product headwinds:** The self-service motion is weak — the website directs all prospects to a demo call, suggesting manual, high-touch onboarding that constrains top-of-funnel velocity. The product relies on voice AI calling carriers, a workflow that many carriers find intrusive; carrier pick-up rates for unknown AI callers are an unproven variable. Performance claims (60–80% loads booked via AI-sourced capacity, 8–10% better buy rates, $50 more margin/load) are self-reported with no independent verification. Testimonials on the site appear generic and may not represent all customers.

**Execution risks:** Lanesurf is a 2025-founded company with 11 employees. It is in the earliest stage of building a go-to-market function (currently hiring its first SDR/BDR). The LDi network rollout across 130+ offices is a meaningful early signal, but dependency on a small number of early enterprise accounts creates revenue concentration risk. Founders (Pratham Bansal, Sarthak Singh Chauhan) are strong technical operators from IIT Delhi with ML backgrounds but have no prior logistics industry experience, raising questions about enterprise sales depth and domain credibility.

**Funding/economic/geopolitical exposure:** No disclosed funding round beyond the YC S25 batch (typically $500K standard). The US trucking market is cyclically sensitive — freight recessions (like 2023–2024) compress broker margins and reduce willingness to spend on new software. Trade policy volatility (tariffs, cross-border flows) can cause sharp volume swings that stress AI systems trained on historical data. There is no indication of international exposure that introduces geopolitical risk directly.

**Defensibility:** The AI voice/email/text stack is replicable by well-funded competitors; Lanesurf's moat depends on proprietary carrier relationship data and self-improving models trained on real call logs. This data flywheel is real but early. Customers can churn to a competitor or build in-house if the broker is large enough. SOC 2 Type II certification is a check-box positive but standard for the category.
